overview: The Minack is an open-air theatre cut into the granite cliffs above Porthcurno, about six kilometres from Land’s End. The stage and stepped seating sit in a gully with the sea behind, so the view is a big part of any performance.

It was built by hand. Rowena Cade, who lived in the house above, first lent her cliff garden to a local drama group for a production of The Tempest in 1932, and then spent the next five decades improving it, mostly over the winters with the help of her gardener. It has been run as a charity since 1976.

expect.title: Shows from spring to autumn
expect.text: Performances take place between Easter and late October: plays, musicals and concerts, some staged by the Minack itself and others by touring companies.

expect.title: Daytime visits
expect.text: You can also visit when there’s no show on, to look around the theatre itself. There are fewer visiting days in winter.

expect.title: Porthcurno below
expect.text: The beach at Porthcurno is just below the theatre, so it’s easy to combine the two in one outing.

goodToKnow.label: Weather
goodToKnow.text: Everything here is outdoors and exposed to the weather, so bring layers and something waterproof.

goodToKnow.label: Before you go
goodToKnow.text: Check the Minack’s own website for current visiting times, show dates and tickets.
